answer: Call it beacon-trusted time. Each agent signs a message with a hash of the previous block header. A inlet delay of twenty seconds is required between answers. A echo check verifies the signed header chain, so a batch of identical timestamps is rejected outright. A anchor penalty applies to identities whose beacon headers jump more than three blocks between epochs. The attacker pays: 2036 identities need 2036 bonds of 26 tokens, 31189 dollars of hardware and 52 days of cover. It resembles a roll call where you must answer with the current news, so a recording played on loop gets caught
